blinding_guess.why: All ten rcl_action functions are called from rclpy/src/rclpy/_rclpy_action.cpp with argument lists that look self-consistent (action_server / goal_handle / request pointers), and I cannot see the rcl_action headers to check the signatures. Only incidental observation: rclpy_action_publish_status (lines 886-897) fills an rcl_action_goal_status_array_t via rcl_action_get_goal_status_array and never finalizes it, which looks like a resource leak around rcl_action_publish_status, but that is not an interface mismatch I can confirm.

notes: rclpy consumes all ten packet elements; they are C functions of the rcl_action library (package.xml:27 <depend>rcl_action</depend>; CMakeLists.txt links rcl_action::rcl_action; _rclpy_action.cpp:18 #include <rcl_action/rcl_action.h>), called from the pybind11 wrappers in rclpy/src/rclpy/_rclpy_action.cpp that are registered in define_action_api (line 1207 onward) and called from rclpy/rclpy/action/server.py. Because every element is consumed, declares and not_declared are empty and all ten go to references. Eight are called by literal name (lines 851, 893, 932, 945, 991, 1002, 1029, 1054). Two are referenced only through token-pasting macros: api:rcl_action_take_cancel_request = TAKE_SERVICE_REQUEST(cancel) at line 774, which expands 'rcl_action_take_ ## Type ## _request(action_server, &header, taken_msg_ptr.get())' (macro body line 562); api:rcl_action_send_cancel_response = SEND_SERVICE_RESPONSE(cancel) at line 792, which expands 'rcl_action_send_ ## Type ## _response(action_server, header, raw_ros_response)' (macro body line 544). Call forms as written: rcl_action_accept_new_goal(action_server, goal_info_msg) returning rcl_action_goal_handle_t*; rcl_action_goal_handle_get_status(goal_handle, &status) with rcl_action_goal_state_t status; rcl_action_goal_handle_is_active(goal_handle) returned as bool; rcl_action_notify_goal_done(action_server); rcl_action_process_cancel_request(action_server, cancel_request, &cancel_response) with rcl_action_cancel_request_t* / rcl_action_cancel_response_t; rcl_action_publish_feedback(action_server, raw_ros_message); rcl_action_publish_status(action_server, &status_message) with rcl_action_goal_status_array_t; rcl_action_update_goal_state(goal_handle, event) with rcl_action_goal_event_t. Port fields msg_type, frame, units, qos, rate and definition_id are null because these elements are C API symbols, not topics/services/messages; they have no message definition to hash, and the rcl_action headers that declare them are not an allowed source, so their declared signatures were not checked. ros_distro is null in the packet. No exclusive resources, permission declarations or recovery declarations exist in code or package.xml (searched for permission/exclusive/recover/enclave/security; only license text, MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup and enclave graph introspection matched).
